purpose: Track acknowledged audit findings across rounds so already-triaged issues are not rediscovered as new blockers without new evidence.

auditSessions.summary: Vault-focused audit did not confirm a new standalone Vault money/stuck bug requiring a contract patch. Pending records, ACK/bounce/fail restoration, stale publish tombstones, and bounded invalid signed external request charging are present in the current implementation.
auditSessions.currentDecision: No Vault contract patch proposed from this session.
notFindings: External session maxCharge greater than canonical expected max charge is not treated as a Vault bug under the current PWA-controlled surcharge/pricing policy.
Raw manual overpay in direct user messages is not treated as a contract finding when it does not break protocol accounting.
Duplicate created_at in the source-level receive intent view is cosmetic only for this audit scope.

carriedVerificationItems.summary: creditActivityAirdrop credits internal user ATH and decrements the remaining airdrop counter; final genesis/deployment evidence must prove the official Vault ATH wallet is funded for the full airdrop allocation.

Vault can only refund the TON value it actually receives from CapsuleHub ACK/bounce, capped by the pending/tombstone refundable amount. CapsuleHub ACK/excess value accounting must be verified in the seam audit.

auditSessions.verificationPolicy: These items are not confirmed Vault bugs. Promote them to findings only if a dedicated seam/deployment pass proves a real under-backed or under-refunded path in an official PWA or release flow.

findings.summary: Permissionless ResendDeployedAck can retain caller-funded TON in the item balance when the Registry rejects the ACK, for example after pending mint is already absent. The loss is capped by the current 20_000_000 nanotON resend max.
notP0P1Rationale: Username records and Registry accounting are not corrupted.
Maximum accepted resend value caps the exposure.
findings.currentDecision: Do not bluntly require exact 4_000_000 nanotons because initial Registry deploy uses the same ACK body and intentionally funds item storage with the deploy reserve.
nextActionOptions: Document ResendDeployedAck as caller-funded top-up/recovery behavior.
Split initial deploy ACK from public resend ABI.
Add resend-specific bounded refund semantics with dust-safe behavior.

findings.area: Vault <-> CapsuleHub late ACK after stale prune
findings.summary: If PrunePendingPublish removed a stale PendingPublish and the real CapsuleHub ACK arrived later, Vault rejected it because routing state was gone. The ACK value is bounce:false, so returned TON became raw Vault balance and was not credited to the user.
notP0P1Rationale: Normal Vault -> CapsuleHub publish flow remains passing.
The issue requires delayed ACK/bounce beyond the stale pending TTL.
Forged ACK and forged Vault publish paths remain rejected.
fix: PrunePendingPublish now converts the active PendingPublish record into a compact tombstone in the existing pending_publishes map instead of deleting all routing data.
The tombstone uses session_id == 0 and keeps owner, budget_epoch, nonce, publish_kind, body_hash, refundable cap, and expiry.
Late authenticated CapsuleHub ACK refunds capped returned TON to active message_budget_ton when the epoch is active, otherwise to ton_balance, and credits the activity airdrop.
Late authenticated CapsuleHub bounce refunds capped returned TON without airdrop.
A second PrunePendingPublish after tombstone expiry deletes the tombstone.
findings.currentDecision: Closed in Vault with a compact tombstone. ACK remains non-bounceable; no new persistent map was added, so external publish pre-accept gas stays within the existing signature-check envelope.

findings.summary: CapsuleHub now stores retrievable payload cells. Private cells are exact-size. Public entries store compact PPH1 header bytes plus raw public text body bytes, 1..1024 bytes for both posts and comments. Page boundaries have no stored counters and no first-page price lottery, and sandbox economics show retained non-fee balance remains above configured storage reserve for Vault-only publish paths.
notManualMisuseRationale: The official PWA can send normal max-size text or image payload cells.
The contract accepts max-size payload cells under the current v1 caps.
Publish fees and storage endowments are not currently size-scaled.
Protocol fee accrued in CapsuleHub remains a liability owed to FeeAccumulator while storage rent is paid from the same physical balance.
findings.currentDecision: Closed for canonical PWA v1 payloads by exact-size private CapsuleHub gates, bounded public payload gates, and dedicated storage-economics evidence. Hash-only delivery remains forbidden.
fix: Public publish validation now stores compact PPH1 header bytes separately from raw body text, so both posts and comments expose a full 1..1024 body bytes instead of padding to private capsule size.
Private publish bodies and headers remain exact-size: header0 104 bytes, header1 30 bytes, standard body 1140 bytes, hybrid body 2228 bytes.
Per-page storage charging was removed from publish pricing; clients can derive page windows from sequential entry ids.
Direct user publish ABI was removed; public and private publishes now enter CapsuleHub only through Vault so ATH discounts apply consistently.
A dedicated storage-economics harness verifies retained non-fee balance remains above configured storage reserve after transaction fees and ACK sends.

findings.summary: Non-basechain ATH deposit and withdrawal paths could become stuck or lossy because wallet derivation allowed other workchains while value envelopes were basechain-sized.
fix: Vault rejects non-basechain AthTransferNotification sender_wallet before ledger credit.
Vault rejects non-basechain WithdrawAth sender and recipient before user ATH debit or pending state.
ATHWallet owner-facing transfer, notify-transfer, and mint-notify transfer reject non-basechain source, recipient, or response paths before token debit.
findings.currentDecision: ATH user paths are basechain-only for this release. This is not full cross-workchain support.

findings.area: Vault <-> ATHWallet stale notification prune and duplicate query reuse
findings.summary: If Vault processed an ATH deposit notification but the ACK reached the official ATH wallet after pending prune, a later real transfer with the same source/query could become unclaimable backing because Vault treated it as a duplicate without crediting it.
fix: PruneStaleNotification records the notification id as processed before deleting pending state.
PruneStaleNotification records a pruned ACK tombstone keyed by query and sender key.
AthTransferNotificationAck is idempotent for a pruned tombstone with matching amount.
findings.currentDecision: Closed at ATHWallet notification state-machine layer. Vault-only handling is insufficient once the official ATH wallet forgets a processed notification id.

findings.area: BuybackBurn <-> ATHWallet low route notification value
findings.summary: A valid STON.fi ATH output with notify value accepted by ATHWallet but below BuybackBurn immediate-burn minimum could leave BuybackBurn stuck in PENDING_STONFI_SWAP.
fix: BuybackBurn accepts authenticated low-value ATH output after sender, query, source, and amount checks pass.
BuybackBurn sends AthTransferNotificationAck to the official ATH wallet so the received ATH remains held by the official wallet.
BuybackBurn records the amount in ath_burn_retry_due_atomic and terminalizes the swap cycle so RetryAthBurnDue can burn it with caller-funded TON.
findings.currentDecision: On-chain recovery is required because this can occur in the honest STON.fi route output flow, not only in manual misuse.

findings.area: BuybackBurn <-> ATHWallet <-> ATHMaster unsupported ATHMaster workchain
findings.summary: A masterchain or unsupported ATHMaster in production genesis could leave BuybackBurn stuck in PENDING_ATH_BURN because official ATH wallet burn forwarding can fail before ATHBurnFailed reaches BuybackBurn.
fix: BuybackBurn init remains unchanged by policy; unsupported deployment topology is not a PWA user flow.
Mainnet genesis verifier rejects non-basechain ATHMaster evidence for the current release.
Final genesis evidence must show buyback_burn.ath_master_address is workchain 0.
regressionCoverage: tests/mainnet-genesis-verify.test.ts::rejects unsupported masterchain ATHMaster in final mainnet genesis evidence
findings.currentDecision: Closed at release-verification layer instead of adding unsupported-workchain policy to BuybackBurn init.

findings.area: UsernameRegistry <-> ATHWallet <-> ATHMaster unsupported ATHMaster workchain
findings.summary: A masterchain or unsupported ATHMaster in production genesis could leave FlushBurnAthDue pending forever because official Registry ATH wallet burn forwarding can fail before ATHBurnFinalized or ATHBurnFailed reaches UsernameRegistry.
fix: UsernameRegistry init remains unchanged by policy; unsupported deployment topology is not a PWA user flow.
Mainnet genesis verifier rejects non-basechain ATHMaster evidence for UsernameRegistry in the current release.
Final genesis evidence must show username_registry.ath_master_address is workchain 0.
regressionCoverage: tests/mainnet-genesis-verify.test.ts::rejects unsupported masterchain ATHMaster in final mainnet genesis evidence
findings.currentDecision: Closed at release-verification layer instead of adding unsupported-workchain policy to UsernameRegistry init.
